judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's mathematical claims check out -- the ordered corner counts (3, 4, 6 fewest-to-most in problem 5 and 6, 4, 3, 0 most-to-fewest in problem 7) and the rule for Ana's top group in problem 8 ('shapes with four straight sides', verify id 8 compare [4, 3] '>' plus a manual entry for the rule) are all correct, and this is the one case in my batch that splits its find-and-explain items properly: problems 3, 6, 8 each carry BOTH a compare entry and a separate manual entry with a specific desc. What the judge missed is the delivered Quick Answers bank. It prints '1. -  2. -  3. -  4. -  6. -  8. -  9. -  10. -' -- eight of ten rows are dashes, and only 9 and 10 are manual-only. Rows 1, 2 and 4 have no manual entry at all: they are pure verified relations ('>', '<', '>') printing the glyph reserved for unchecked work. A grader gets a usable quick answer for exactly two problems (5 and 7) on a ten-problem sheet, and cannot tell which dashes mean 'checked' and which mean 'read the key'. That is a real answer_key_quality defect behind a 4.

strengths_to_preserve: Problems 3, 6 and 8 model the correct verification split that most sheets in this run get wrong: the countable part is a compare entry (3 = 3 for the tiny and huge triangles, 4 = 4 for the square flat and on its point, 4 > 3 for Ana's groups) and the reasoning part is a separate manual entry with a concrete desc. Preserve this pattern verbatim as the reference example.

The answer key's rejection criteria are specific rather than generic: on problem 8 it says not to accept 'they are all boxes' because one of the shapes is a trapezoid, and on problem 3 to accept any answer naming sides or corners but not 'because it looks like a triangle'.
Problem 7 deliberately includes a shape with zero straight sides so the ordering 6, 4, 3, 0 forces the child to treat 'no straight sides' as a countable attribute rather than a missing value.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sends string expecteds through bare sympy.sympify; relation strings raise and fall back to '---', the same text render_entry returns for a manual-only problem. On a worksheet whose verification is dominated by compare/relation entries this empties most of the bank and destroys the verified/manual distinction.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: rows 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10 all print '-'.
verify.json ids 1, 2, 4 are compare/relation with expecteds '>', '<', '>' and carry NO manual entry, yet render as '-'.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py lines 57-61 (sympify fallback) and lines 73-74 (manual-only fallback) return the same '---'.

root_causes.description: Compare entries verify only the relation; the operands the student is told to write are carried in 'values' as inputs and never checked as printed answers. Every counting problem on this sheet asks for two numerals AND a mark, and is covered by one entry.
evidence: Problem 1: 'Count the straight sides of shape A and shape B. Write the two numbers, then circle the shape that has MORE sides' -> single entry compare [4, 3] '>'.
Problem 4: 'how many did you circle, and how many did you leave? Circle the bigger number' -> single entry compare [4, 3] '>'.

Problem 8: 'how many sides does every shape in the TOP row have? ... Write the two numbers and circle the bigger one' -> compare [4, 3] '>' plus the rule's manual entry; the two numerals themselves are unverified.

improvements.title: Render verified relations in the Quick Answers bank and stop reusing the manual dash for them
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, handle relation strings ('<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '!=') before the sympify call and typeset them with the entry's 'values' (e.g. '$4 > 3$'), and give manual-only rows a distinct marker such as 'see key' so the two meanings are visually separable. On this sheet that turns eight dashes into two.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_render_quick_answers.py: render_entry for a compare/relation entry must return text containing the relation and must differ from the manual-only marker; and a mixed problem (compare + manual, like id 3 here) must show the verified relation rather than collapsing to a dash. Fails today, passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: The bank becomes usable for a whole class of geometry and comparison worksheets whose answers are relations rather than numbers, and a grader can once again tell verified rows from manual ones.
improvements.risk: Longer bank entries reduce column_count from four to three, so answer-key page budget needs re-checking on the largest sheets.

improvements.title: Verify the operand numerals a compare problem asks the student to write, not just the relation
improvements.proposed_change: Make coverage slot-level in SKILL.md and enforce it in tests/check_layout.py by counting rendered answer-location macros per \problem body against the expecteds bound to that id. For compare items whose prose says 'write the two numbers', additionally require read_data or eval entries for each operand so the counts a child actually writes are checked, rather than being trusted as inputs inside 'values'.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem prints two numeral slots plus a relation slot and carries a single compare entry: the gate must exit non-zero. Passes today (this is exactly problems 1, 2, 4 and 8 here); after the fix only the three-entry version passes.
improvements.expected_impact: Side and corner counts read off a figure -- the values everything else on the sheet depends on -- become machine-checked instead of implicit.
improvements.risk: Verify files across the corpus need back-filling, and for figure-derived counts the entries are only as good as the figure, so the facet still leans on tests/check_prose_consistency.py for figure/JSON agreement.

case_summary: The strongest verification design in my batch: every explanation and drawing (problems 3, 6, 8, 9, 10) is flagged manual with concrete grading criteria, and every countable claim is a compare entry, so the sheet honestly separates what was checked from what needs an adult. The mathematics is correct throughout and the defining-versus-non-defining framing (colour, size, orientation held constant against sides and corners) is exactly on target for K.G / 1.G. The damage is in delivery: because eight of ten Quick Answers rows print '-', including three pure verified relations, the printed key hides the very verification the case did well. Slot-level coverage is the secondary gap -- 'write the two numbers, then circle' is one entry, not three.
